app.title: EarthSense: drivers and climate links of surface solar radiation trends
app.summary: A person starts from a world map coloured by the modelled trend in surface solar radiation. They click one grid cell or drag a rectangle over a region. For that place, the interface shows how much each atmospheric input contributed to the trend, plots the smoothed and normalised yearly series of the inputs and of other climate variables against the radiation series, and fills a table of correlations, trend sizes and significance, with strong values coloured. The person can hide series in the legends and type notes. They download the contributions, drivers and climate series for that place as CSV files.

task.text: Pick a location or region on a global trend map and see which atmospheric drivers account for its surface radiation trend and how other climate variables move with it.

data.text: Gridded global model output on a latitude-longitude grid: a trend map, per-cell contributions of each input parameter to that trend, and yearly anomaly series of the inputs and of several climate variables.
data.item: a latitude-longitude grid cell, or a rectangular region of cells, with its yearly series

stage.text: analysing gridded radiative transfer output to attribute decadal trends to their drivers

mechanism.text: A raster map acts as the selector: a click on a cell or a box drag over a region recomputes, on the server, a cosine-latitude-weighted regional mean. That mean feeds a contribution bar chart, two line charts of smoothed normalised yearly series, a statistics table and CSV download links, all for the selected place.

field.text: trend attribution of radiative transfer model output in climate science

workflow.name: pick a place on a map and break its trend into contributing factors

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A global raster of the decadal trend in surface solar radiation, with a diverging colour bar and coastlines. Hovering shows a cell's lon, lat and trend.
Clicking a grid cell selects one point. Dragging a persistent box selects a region, which is averaged with cosine-of-latitude weights. A readout shows the position and its trend.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Bars show each atmospheric input's contribution to the trend (cloud cover, cloud optical thickness, aerosol, water vapour, ozone…), next to a hatched bar for the total trend

Yearly series of the drivers and of the climate variables are Savitzky-Golay filtered, normalised, spline-smoothed and overlaid with the radiation series. Clicking a legend entry hides a series, and hovering shows the raw anomalies with units.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A table gives each variable's Pearson and Spearman correlation with radiation, its Theil-Sen change over the period and a linear-regression p-value. |r| ≥ 0.6 is shown in red, and significant increases or decreases in green or orange.
Three links appear after a selection: 'Get Contributions', 'Get Drivers' and 'Get Climate'. Each downloads a CSV, with the coordinates or region bounds in the file name.

distinctive: The selection can be a single grid cell or a dragged region, and regional values are area-weighted by the cosine of latitude
The total trend is split into additive per-parameter contributions shown next to the total as a hatched bar
Series are filtered, standardised and spline-smoothed so variables in very different units share one axis, while the tooltip still shows raw anomalies with units
The statistics table colours rows by preset thresholds for strong correlation and significant trend direction
